![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097009/assets/1c42152de7cf176fa122ddf48aad7d93fe982ec1bc2717e3048d9ff5ea45f302.png)

The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Given $g(t)={\int }_{1}^{t}f(x)\,\text{d}x,$ determine the value of $g(6).$
worked_solution:
Evaluating $g(t)$ at $t=6,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
g(6)={\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral gives the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097009/assets/145d9c16e27c67876d1ae2a00dce15b3cb7437f6a9121971fe4434e6c1fe943c.png)

Note that the graph above consists of $2$ parts:

- $x\in [1,2],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a trapezoid. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{1}.$

- $x\in [2,6],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a triangle. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{2}.$

Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
g(6)={\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

Now, let's compute these integrals:

- To find the first integral where $x\in [1,2],$ we compute the area ${A}_{1}$ of the trapezoid as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot (1+2) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the second integral where $x\in [2,6],$ we compute the area ${A}_{2}$ of the triangle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}g(6)={\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}+4=\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
